$comment: Model IDs are config, never hard-coded in source. Swapping the writing model must require no code change (F14 AC).

sources.note: claude-haiku-5-5 capabilities, for the review bench (issue #58).
quality_reviewer role added: claude-haiku-5-5 confirmed current (adaptive thinking, default effort medium). Prices re-checked on the pricing page the same day, unchanged.

writer.why: Placeholder default per IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md s0. FINAL CHOICE IS THE OWNER'S, from the F14 bake-off. Override with WRITING_MODEL env.

helper.why: All cheap structured steps: normalize, L2 input classifier, L4 safety review, bible update, JSON repair.

quality_reviewer.why: Owner approved 2026-10-15 (issue #58, DECISIONS #201). The F7 quality review only. On the review bench, Haiku 5.5 with its default adaptive thinking (effort medium) had 0 format failures in 1,232 reviews against 2-10% on Haiku 4.5, and agreed with the hand labels on 64-83% of the train half against 31-56%. With thinking off it is no better than Haiku 4.5, so thinking stays on. The safety review and the other helper steps stay on the helper until each has its own eval.

factpack.why: Needs the web_search server tool; Haiku 4.5 does not support web_search_20260209. Runs once per topic.

judge_primary.why: OWNER'S DECISION, 2026-09-27. JUDGE_AGENT.md s2 asks for the strongest available model; the owner chose Opus 5.5 over Fable 5.1, which halves the judging cost of a bake-off ($16.90 vs $40.44) at the price of a slightly weaker primary instrument. Fable 5.1 remains the SECOND judge on the highest-stakes comparisons, so the strongest model still cross-checks the verdicts that decide the outcome.

pr_reviewer.why: The PR reviewer agent (issue #13, DECISIONS #151). Read by .github/workflows/pr-review.yml with jq; runs on the owner's subscription, never through callModel(). As capable as the model that writes the code.

judge_secondary.why: JUDGE_AGENT.md s6 step 5: a second judge on the 12 highest-stakes comparisons, with the agreement rate reported. Now the strongest model, which keeps s2's intent alive where it matters most. Both judges are also contestants, so self-preference bias is reported on their own rows rather than engineered away - see DECISIONS.md #3.

claude-fable-5-1.notes: Thinking always on: omit the thinking param entirely; {type:'disabled'} and budget_tokens both 400. tool_choice any/tool return 400.

claude-haiku-4-5-20251001.notes: Does NOT support the effort parameter (errors). Uses the older tokenizer, so token counts are ~30% lower than the 4.7+ models for identical text - bake-off cost must reconcile against measured generation_logs, not computed estimates. We send no thinking config: helper tasks are structured extraction and need none.

claude-haiku-5-5.notes: Released 2026-10-07. Adaptive thinking is ON by default, steered by effort; omit temperature/top_p/top_k (400). About 30% more tokens than Haiku 4.5 for the same text. Whether it accepts thinking {type:'disabled'} is probed in the review bench, not documented on the overview page.
